recipes.name: Doc's Best Beef Jerky
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds beef round steak, cut into thin strips

steps.text: Prepare the marinade: Combine soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, liquid smoke, brown sugar, salt, pepper, meat tenderizer, garlic powder, onion powder, and paprika in a glass bowl.
Place beef strips in a 9x13-inch glass baking dish. Pour marinade over top; toss until evenly coated. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 8 hours or overnight.
Remove beef strips from the bowl and place between two pieces of plastic wrap; pound to 1/8-inch thickness.
Arrange pounded beef strips in a single layer on the trays of a dehydrator. Dry at the dehydrator's highest setting until jerky is done to your liking, at least 4 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Doc's Best Beef Jerky
raw_recipe.description: An easy, homemade beef jerky marinade, made with soy sauce, liquid smoke, brown sugar, and spices, makes the most flavorful beef jerky ever — maybe even the best you'd ever had!

video.description: In this video, learn how to make homemade beef jerky flavored with soy sauce, liquid smoke, brown sugar, and spices. Start with a round steak, and cut it into thin strips. Then apply the marinade, and let it soak. Finally, you’ll need to dehydrate the meat with a dehydrator, or you can use an oven or air fryer with the correct settings. Store the finished product in an airtight container or resealable bags, and grab a wholesome snack whenever the urge strikes.

review.reviewBody: Loved this recipe, very tasty and tender. I cooked it in the oven on a rack at 180 two and a half hours. Will make this one again. GOOD, GOOD, GOOD

This recipe is soooo good!! I've never made anything like this before and couldn't believe how easy it was! I have a butcher cut the meat so I don't have to. I use gallon zip lock bags to put the marinade in, add the meat, and throw it back in the fridge. I use this for 1.5 pounds of meat and it's still great. I make a few batches at a time, so just keep the marinade in the bag until I want to use it. I've left it in the fridge marinating for a couple days and it wasn't overpowering. I use my air fryer because it has a dehydrator function, it's SUPER easy. The only thing I changed was not adding the salt and a little less liquid smoke, but everything else was perfect. My husband loves it so much I'm making 4 batches today. Honestly it tastes just as good if not better than store bought, I don't think I'll ever buy beef jerky again!

Used Jerky gun for ground turkey and decided on second batch to omit liquid smoke. Used hickory on Traeger for 4 hours and turned out wonderful. 
These do not last as everyone in the house eats them.

I like this jerky recipe very much, reminds me of the hickory farms beef jerky we used to get when I was a kid. And I've been missing that! I only gave it four stars because I did it a little differently from the recipe here. I didn't use meat tenderizer, I don't like using msg and I believe that is what it is. I used gluten free low sodium tamari for the soy and I also cut down the salt by about half. The first couple times I made it I didn't have liquid smoke so I used chipotle powder which was too spicy and didn't mix well. I also used the amounts in the recipe for one pound of meat. I would double the recipe for two pounds of meat. 
 I was using this without the liquid smoke and it was ok but it's better with the hickory flavored smoke I used today. And I warmed the marinade on the stove and then let it cool to get the ingredients well incorporated. I found that mixing everything room temperature, I couldn't get everything dissolved and parts of the jerky would be more flavorful or more spicy than others. Warming the marinade allowed the brown sugar to dissolve and all the other ingredients to incorporate well. Once that was cool which didn’t take long, I added it to the meat, mixed it well and let it marinate for about 12 hours in the fridge. I used my oven to dry it, 180 degrees which is the lowest it goes, for about 4 hours. 
 With these changes, I'm very happy with the recipe and will be using it again. I shared it with friends that really liked it also.

I tried this recipe with a couple variations.
1.) I used venison
2.) I marinated it for 30 hours
3.) I eliminated the liquid smoke and meat tenderizer, then dried it in the smoker using apple wood.
4.) I didn't pound it thin. I prefer a thicker meatier jerky.
5.) I separated the marinade and the meat to two bowls and added about four tablespoons of pureed scotch bonnets to one of the bowls. (It was spicy, but not unbearable).

My only regret is that I didn't make more. I took the batch to work and only got one piece for myself. everybody that tried it came back for more.

Just tried making my first beef jerky with on my Instant Pot Duo Crisp. This is such an awesome recipe! I did use Mesquite liquid smoke and omitted the meat tenderizer. The top round beef I used was already sliced thinly. I marinated it for 4 hours. It turned out so good I’ll probably keep making these!

Wonderful recipe!
I used Bragg's Aminos instead of soy sauce, and added 1/2 teaspoon mustard powder, then baked the strips in my oven at 180F for 3 1/2 hours. I will be making this again.

My son just started college and I wanted to send him some homemade "love" in his care package. I chose this recipe, and I am so glad I did. First time making jerky so I didn't dare change anything! I can honestly say, I never will make any changes either. I used two types of beef: London broil and top round. I much prefer London broil. The London broil cut was free of any fat or connective tissue which made the jerky's texture very consistent. I placed the meat on 3 cookie sheets topped with racks. I baked it in my oven set to 170 with the door propped open about 1/2" with a kitchen towel. Steam still collected on the oven door and I just wiped it dry occasionally.
I started removing pieces of jerky from the oven after about 4 hours. The larger pieces and the ones that were closer to the middle of the baking sheet took about 5.5 hrs. The most helpful review stated to let the jerky cool completely before testing to see if it's done. I doubled the recipe and 4 lbs of beef yielded 1.5 lbs of delicious jerky. If my son doesn't absolutely love this, he will be up for adoption. Thank you for the recipe and all of the helpful reviews.

I substituted some ingredients, like duck sauce in place of sugar and sprinkled some Japanese BBQ rub to the marinade to give it a different flavor. After making the first batch at 165 for 4 hours, I toned it down slightly to 160 for 4 hours and it came out perfectly cooked. PS: I left out the tenderizer and smoke. Easy recipe and will try again with other rubs.

I was looking for a beef jerky recipe to try as I am on the keto diet and wanted jerky that wasn't packed with sugar. I found Doc's recipe and figured I could swap out the brown sugar for a sweetener/maple extract substitute. It worked! I tripled the recipe to use with 3 pounds of a mix of top and bottom round. I cut the table salt in half (after tripling the original amount) and it turned out to just the right saltiness for my palette. I marinated for a day and a half using gallon-sized ziplock baggies and then dehydrated til done (my dehydrator is OLD so no temp setting or timer lol). The texture is different than store bought, but in a very good way. I'm hoping there will be enough when we leave to go backpacking because my husband won't stay out of it! Will definitely add this to my have-to-make again box!

Fantastic jerky. I buy a bottom round roast and my butcher slices it thin for me (costs a little bit more to get it sliced jerky thin but it is WELL WORTH IT). I cut it into jerkly length strips with a pair of cutlery scissors. I follow the receipe to the letter except I substitute low sodium soy sauce, hot paparika, and curing salt for those three ingrediants. I let it marinate for three days and then put it in the dehydrater for 3 to 4 hours. I have had many rave reviews on it and get asked when am I making another batch. I just put on a 6 pound batch to marinate.
I have used this recipe as is for years! It is the best jerky recipe out there. I'm making jerky as I write
make enough to last us as a snack throughout the whole month. Everyone loves it in my house hold
Followed the recipe to the T and its ridiculously salty. 2 lbs of meat wasted.

Are you the Doc from in Jacksonville nc? I worked at sanders ford. I would leave money in the mail box for you. 300-400 a month I was buying!!! lol if you are one, I’d like to get back in contact with you too you need to drop that spicy version that you have! That beef jerky is freaking amazing.

Made it once before and loved it. I marinated for 2 days to really get the flavours through the meat, then used my dehydrator. It only took about 4 hours to dry. I substitute salt with MSG for that umami kick! I'm British and like Marmite - IYKYN!
great recipe, found it made it, everyone loved it. i have tried other, but i always come back to this one. This is the one everyone ask's me to make.
Easy to make and tastes great!

So some people are saying WAY TOO MUCH SALT. I made this recipe multiple times and it was delicious. The only thing I can think of that may have happened with people’s jerky being too salty. Is that they might have used a TABLESPOON of salt instead of a TEASPOON of salt. That would definitely make a difference and ruin the taste for sure.
This my second time around. Both times I missed the paprika because it's not on the list of ingredients for the marinade. Should it be? I'm old. It's an entitlement. 😁
